🇺🇸🇷🇺 US and Russia strip AI safeguards from UN autonomous weapons text – Washington Post

The US and Russia pushed through the removal of key restrictions on the military use of AI from a UN draft on lethal autonomous weapons, The Washington Post reports, citing negotiation participants and documents it reviewed.

At the Geneva talks, the delegations reportedly removed:

➡️the requirement that a human review AI-selected targets before a strike;

➡️provisions requiring ethical considerations;

➡️language requiring such systems to operate "predictably" and "reliably."

According to WaPo, on the final day of talks the American and Russian delegations spent about 15 hours reworking the document. Each fielded a team of roughly ten lawyers, almost twice the size of other delegations.

The talks are part of a UN effort to set international rules for lethal autonomous systems that can select and engage targets on their own. The agreed text is non-binding. Countries will meet again in Geneva in November to decide whether to open negotiations on a full international treaty. More than 70 states back the text as a basis for binding rules, but the process runs on consensus. Washington and Moscow both oppose legally binding limits, so they can effectively block it.

The technology is already in use. In March, WaPo reported that the US military relied on Anthropic's Claude, integrated into Palantir's Maven Smart System, to suggest and prioritize targets and generate coordinates as it struck around 1,000 targets in the first 24 hours of the war on Iran.

🇮🇷 Iran completes mega railway giving Afghanistan its shortest route to world’s oceans
 
Tracklaying along the new 730 km-long Chabahar-Zahedan Railway has been completed, linking Iran’s only oceanic port to the intersection of its border with Afghanistan and Pakistan.

Workers are now finishing station buildings and signalling systems, and doing safety tests, with the railway set to come online in early 2027.
 
Engineering feat

The railway navigates the mountainous, seismically active terrain of Sistan and Baluchestan. To build it, engineers constructed 39 tunnels stretching 17 km, 201 bridges, and ~2k special drainage structures under tracks to prevent flash flood washouts.

One of the most sophisticated projects of its kind regionally, the railway boasts ~90% Iranian materials and knowhow.

Once up and running, the line will move people and freight at speeds up to 120 and 90 km/h, respectively.
 
Strategic significance

➡️  Besides being a boon for local exporters, the railway can give Afghanistan its best means to ship goods globally (using the existing Khaf-Herat route, already linked to Iran’s grid, or building a direct line to Zahedan). Recovering from US occupation, Afghanistan can provide the world with vast mineral wealth, plus an array of agricultural and artisanal goods.

➡️  Once a ~800 km extension through Mashhad to the Turkmenistan border is complete (work is already underway), the line will provide landlocked Central Asian countries their shortest route to the ocean to ship energy, agricultural commodities, food, metals, minerals and textiles.
